asked_by: Madhav, 27 Oct 2026 09:17 Toronto: "Yes to all your recommendations" (the recommendation, after reviewing his 25-question Ask session of 27 Oct: test the topics Ananta could only answer from the textbook: candlestick patterns, valuation (P/E, P/B), beta and low volatility, option spreads, corporate actions)
title: Corporate actions: do stocks do better after a bonus or split, a buyback, or a large dividend, from the ex-date on?
hypothesis: Bonus issues and splits signal management confidence and widen ownership; buybacks signal the shares are cheap; a large dividend signals strong cash flow: each is followed by better 20-60 session returns than ordinary days.

data.events: silver/corporate_actions/record_b.parquet (NSE corporate-action records 2000-2026 with EX-DATES and kinds; there is NO announcement date in the free history, so the test starts at the ex-date, which is known in advance, not at the news)
data.stocks: gold/teachers/stock_panel.parquet, every stock in the panel (liquidity rank 1-500) because buybacks are rare in the liquid 250
data.nothing_sealed: no 2024+ row; nothing was looked at for outcomes before this spec

definitions.dividend_y2: kind DIVIDEND with amount per share >= 2% of the previous session's close (the unadjusted prev_close on the ex-date row of silver/cm_bhavcopy, series EQ; if missing, the event is skipped) [data source fixed before the run, 27 Oct]
definitions.event row: the ex-date session in the panel (matched on symbol and date); one per stock per 10 sessions
definitions.outcome: panel fwd20 / fwd60: from the NEXT session's open (the day after the ex-date), adjusted prices

statistics.test: india.teachers_stock.level against every 5th session of the panel in the same quarter, t across quarters (quarters need 3 events)
statistics.periods: development to 2017, validation 2018-2023; nothing from 2024 on, no sealed folder
statistics.verdict: india/registry.record standard rule; 16 blocks per period

bar.note: family 'events' (24) plus these 5; k frozen at 29

not_claimed: No paper rule changes. Announcement-day reactions cannot be tested: the free history has ex-dates only.
